intent.title: Use the existing cards and mods as the browser behaviour baseline
intent.quote: But I Guess it should be the same behavior as it is the case now with cards and mods.
intent.question: How should coding-agent integration work for the browser issue-resolution UI?
intent.readback: Use the existing Plumb cards and Claude mod interaction as the behavioural baseline for the browser: present issues and their resolution choices, apply the owner's answer through Plumb, and carry any follow-up into the agent workflow. The browser-to-agent connection and location of follow-up conversation still need to be chosen.
will: Preserve the meaning and effects of existing card actions.
Preserve the connection between issue resolution and agent follow-up.
Improve the browser presentation for understanding and resolving each issue type.
wont: Invent a different agent autonomy policy merely because the interface moves to a browser.
assumptions: Behavioural parity is the baseline, with gaps in actual resolution tracked explicitly.
The precise way a browser connects to the relevant coding-agent session remains to be evaluated.

decisions.title: Base browser resolution behaviour on existing cards and mods
decisions.question: What behaviour should browser issue resolution follow?
decisions.chosen: Use existing Plumb card and mod behaviour as the baseline, including the connection to agent follow-up.
alternatives: Create a separate issue-resolution agent with a new autonomy model.
Build an approval-only browser disconnected from agent follow-up.
decisions.rationale: The owner suggested preserving current card/mod behaviour after reopening coding-agent integration.
